sentences.text: The claim of appellant/claimants before the Tribunal, in brief, was that on 09.05.2012 deceased Bhanu Pratap Patel was carefully driving Santro Car bearing registration No.CG 06 C 0702 which was owned by respondent no.1 Amar Singh Patel.
In the said car Devnandan Patel was also sitting.

It is stated that in front of Guru Tej Bahadur Rice Mill situated near Mahasamund to Bagbahra road,
on National Highway No.353, the front tyre of the car suddenly burst due to which the car became out of control and collided with a tree, as a result of which, Bhanu Pratap suffered grievous injuries on his chest, ribs and knee.
He was immediately taken to District Hospital Mahasamund and then to Balaji Super Speciality Hospital, Raipur where he died during the course of treatment.
A report in this regard was lodged to Police Station Mahasamund (CG).
3. It is claimed that at the time of accident, deceased Bhanu Pratap was aged around 40 years and was earning Rs.3,300/- by working as a driver.
Due to the casual death of deceased Bhanu Pratap Patel, there is an irreparable loss to the claimants who are the wife, children and parents of the deceased.

Therefore, the claimants preferred an application under Section 163A of the Motor Vehicles Act before the Claims Tribunal claiming total Neutral Citation 2024:CGHC:17185 compensation of Rs.9,02,200/-.
4.
The learned Tribunal, after considering the evidence and documents available on record, assessed the income of the deceased at Rs.3,000/- per month i.e. Rs.36,000/- per annum.
Since the claimants are the wife, children and parents of the deceased, 1/4th of the income was deducted towards personal expenses and after deduction, the amount comes to Rs.27,000/- per annum.
Considering the fact that the deceased was aged around 40 years, multiplier of 15 was applied and the total loss of dependency worked out to Rs.4,05,000/-.

In addition, Rs.5,000/- for consortium to the wife of deceased, Rs.5,000/- for funeral expenses, Rs.5,000/- for loss of estate and Rs.25,000/-
for love and affection has been awarded.
Accordingly, the Claims Tribunal has awarded total compensation of Rs.4,45,000/- in favour of the claimants with interest @ 6% per annum, from the date of application till its realization.

5. Learned counsel appearing for appellant/claimants submits that the compensation awarded by the Tribunal under other heads is on lower side and needs to be enhanced by an additional amount of Rs.55,000/- taking the total compensation to the limit of Rs.5,00,000/-.

6. On the other hand, it has been argued on behalf of learned counsel for insurance company that in the facts and circumstances of case, the compensation awarded by the Claims Tribunal is just and proper and requires no further enhancement.
7.
Heard counsel for the parties and perused the record.
8. The claim application was preferred by the claimants Neutral Citation 2024:CGHC:17185 before the Tribunal under Section 163A of the Motor Vehicles Act.

The Tribunal has awarded Rs.5,000/-
towards consortium to the wife of deceased, Rs.5,000/- for funeral expenses, Rs.5,000/- for loss of estate and Rs.25,000/- for love and affection, totaling Rs.40,000/- under other heads which as per Smt. making the total compensation as Rs.5,00,000/- (4,45,000 + 55,000).
9. In the result, the appeal is partly allowed.
The appellant/claimants shall be entitled to Rs.55,000/- in addition to what is already awarded by the Claims Tribunal.
The enhanced amount will carry interest @ 6% per annum from the date of enhancement of the award till its realization.
The impugned award stands modified to the above extent and rest of the conditions shall remain intact.

10. The Registry is further directed to communicate the claimants in writing "the enhanced amount"
in this appeal as against the award made by the Tribunal below.

The said communication be made in Hindi Deonagri language and the help of paralegal workers may be availed with a co- ordination of Secretary, Legal Aid of the concerned area wherein the claimants reside.
